title: Token Counter for a Tiny Tokenizer
summary: Split text into word/punctuation tokens and count frequencies — the first step in almost every NLP pipeline.
description:
## Scenario

Before any embedding model or LLM ever sees a document, something has to split it into tokens. Production tokenizers (BPE, WordPiece) are subword-based and complex — but a simple whitespace-and-punctuation tokenizer is still what you reach for when prototyping a keyword search, a frequency-based feature, or a quick text-cleaning step.

## Task

Implement two functions in `solution.py`:

- `tokenize(text: str) -> list[str]` — lowercases the text and splits it into a list of word tokens, stripping punctuation. Words separated by any whitespace become separate tokens. Punctuation attached to a word (commas, periods, etc.) should be removed, not counted as its own token.
- `token_frequencies(tokens: list[str]) -> dict[str, int]` — returns a mapping from token to how many times it appears, preserving first-seen order.

## Requirements

- `tokenize("")` returns `[]`.
- Punctuation (`.`, `,`, `!`, `?`, `:`, `;`, `"`) is stripped from token edges.
- Tokenization is case-insensitive (`"The"` and `"the"` are the same token).
- `token_frequencies` never raises on an empty list — it returns `{}`.
